messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT PAGE: p99 streaming latency spike for customer 'Kumo' on gpool-21. Root cause unknown. Impact: streaming stalls, clients seeing long gaps. Invoked page for oncall.

maria: I'm on it. grabbing logs now. what's the customer id?

diego: Kumo acct id 4921, single-tenant pool. I've got retention traces. p95 stable but p99 jumps ~4x since 14:12 UTC.

maria: confirmed. streaming stalls where chunks stop for ~8-12s intermittently. Errors show 'write timeout to session' in node-agent logs.

charlie: tagging eng-runtime. @samir can you check kv-cache eviction and long prefix cache thrash? Could be prefix-heavy prompts.

samir: looking. KV cache evictions spike concurrent with the p99. eviction_count ~12k/min across gpool-21. Sequence lengths median 600, tail up to 6k.

maria: customer reports a burst of unusually long prompts at 14:11 UTC — customer says "batch summarize" job kicked off. High concurrency from a single tenant.

kumo-cs: (from Kumo support) yes, they started a backfill of older docs. they didn't expect this to hit streaming endpoints but it did. they can pause.

maria: immediate mitigation — please pause the backfill and retry with smaller concurrency. sending customer note now. Also rolling routing policy to route Kumo to spare-dedicated pool gpool-45.

diego: provisioning gpool-45 routing change via feature-flag. Applying policy now.

deploy-bot: routing-change applied for customer=4921 -> gpool-45. rollouts: instant.

maria: after routing, p99 dropped from 9.4s -> 2.2s in next 5 mins. Streaming stalls reduced but a few residual 3-4s gaps remain.

samir: still seeing KV cache churn on gpool-45 but lower. I'm going to enable prefix-preserve cache mode for this customer's sessions (temp config) to avoid thrash.

charlie: good. also enable fallback-model variant "fast-gen-quant" for streaming to reduce per-token compute; degrade quality but preserves latency. Apply as canary (10%).

diego: canary applied. traffic split 10% -> fast-gen-quant. monitoring.

maria: customer paused job. their support confirmed perceived UX improved. we're still within SLO for p95, p99 edging downward.

samir: added temporary rate-limiter at entry for that tenant to cap concurrency at 40 concurrent streaming sessions. will hold for 1 hour.

maria: note to ops: this incident escalates to SEV3 since single-tenant impact but mitigated. Logging ticket for postmortem.

charlie: collecting artifacts: agent logs, kv eviction metrics, routing decisions, model variant logs, and customer timeline. Assigning owners: triage=maria, runtime=samir, routing=diego, postmortem=charlie.

maria: immediate customer message sent: "We've put safeguards and routing in place, please resume when ready. We'll follow up with a postmortem and recommended client-side throttles."

kumo-cs: thanks team. will coordinate restart tomorrow morning in controlled batches.

maria: next steps timeline: 1) follow up with customer — within 1h; 2) generate postmortem draft — by EOD; 3) permanent mitigations: prefix-aware caching, improved tenant circuit breaker profiles, and routing automation — plan in 3 days.

diego: quick command snippets I used:
```bash
# check kv eviction tail
rk metrics query --filter 'gpool=gpool-21,metric=kv_evictions' --since 15m
# apply routing override
rk routing update --customer 4921 --pool gpool-45 --reason 'mitigate tail latency'
```

samir: logs snippet:
```text
[2026-03-15T14:12:05Z] session=xyz write_timeout after 12000ms
[2026-03-15T14:12:05Z] kv_cache: evict key=prefix:abc size=4k
```

maria: should we consider making streaming output flush more aggressive for long prompts as a short-term change? That might reduce perceived stalls.

charlie: yes but test first. aggressive flush could increase CPU. guard with canary.

maria: closing the active page. will reopen if errors recur. tagging for postmortem follow up. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: incident-note: SEV3 resolved — mitigation applied, customer notified. ticket=INC-2026-4921

samir: saving metrics snapshot to /incidents/6969696969/metrics-snapshot.json

diego: adding playbook note: recommend adding a tenant-level concurrency cap and backfill detection alert.

maria: thanks all. good triage and quick routing flip. we'll coordinate PM with product for automation.
